title: Storage duration of human blood samples for fatty acid concentration analyses
author: Mohsen, Peisker, et al.

steps.title: Collect whole blood samples
steps.instruction: Draw six whole‑blood samples from three coronary‑by‑pass patients after induction of anesthesia using an aspiration technique into standard serum tubes (S‑monovette 01.1601, Sarstedt AG & Co. KG, Germany) following institutional peripheral‑vein puncture guidelines.

steps.title: Allow clotting at room temperature
steps.instruction: Leave the collected blood in the monovettes for 20–30 min at room temperature to allow clot formation.

steps.title: Store clotted samples before processing
steps.instruction: Place the clotted monovettes at +4 °C until the scheduled processing times of 6 h, 12 h, 24 h, 48 h, 96 h, and 7 days after collection.

steps.title: Centrifuge and aliquot serum
steps.instruction: At each time point, centrifuge the monovette at 2000 g for 10 min, transfer the serum to labeled cryovials, and store them at –80 °C until lipid extraction.

steps.title: Extract lipids from serum
steps.instruction: For each serum sample, pipette 200 µl into a 6 ml glass vial, add 1 ml methanol, 0.5 ml chloroform, and 100 µl pentadecanoic‑acid (internal standard) dissolved in methanol; vortex and centrifuge for 20 min to pellet debris. Collect the supernatant (extract 1). Re‑treat the pellet twice with fresh chloroform/methanol mixtures (same composition), centrifuging after each addition and collecting supernatants (extract 2 and extract 3). Combine extracts 1‑3 and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Derivatize fatty acids to methyl esters
steps.instruction: When a sample reaches its scheduled analysis point, thaw the stored extract at room temperature, hydrolyze the lipids, and convert fatty acids to methyl esters by adding 1 N methanolic HCl; incubate as required for complete methylation.

steps.title: Analyze DHA by GC‑FID
steps.instruction: Inject the fatty‑acid‑methyl‑ester (FAME) mixture into a gas‑chromatograph equipped with a flame‑ionization detector; identify DHA peaks and quantify DHA concentration by comparing peak area to that of the internal standard pentadecanoic acid.

steps.title: Perform statistical data analysis
steps.instruction: Measure DHA concentration for each time point, conduct a Friedman test comparing each later time point to the 6 h reference, and if a significant difference is found, apply a Wilcoxon test.
